turns.user: Can we buy the 5-litre gaskets from a supplier that doesn't have a food-grade certificate? Their price is much better.
turns.agent: No, we cannot buy the 5-litre gaskets from a supplier without a food-grade certificate. According to Supplier Policy v2.3 §4.1 (POL-SUP-003 §4.1), a supplier of any part that comes into contact with food (including gaskets) must hold a valid food-grade certificate.

KJOSHI.thought: I need to check the purchasing policy regarding food-grade certificates for food-contact parts.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.1 A supplier of any part that comes into contact with food (gaskets, lids, body blanks, and any item marked food-contact in the item master) must hold a food-grade certificate. This is the certificate referred to in Purchase Policy §6.2.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.2 The certificate must be a test report from a laboratory accredited for food-contact materials (for example an FSSAI-notified laboratory), or a BIS conformity certificate for stainless steel grade 304 or better.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.6 The certificate covers the supplier, not a single item. If the supplier changes the material or the compound of a part (for example a new silicone grade), it must give a fresh test report for that part.

clauses.heading: 4. Food-grade certificates
clauses.text: 4.3 The certificate is uploaded in Bahi against the supplier (certificate type FOOD-GRADE) with its document reference and its valid-to date, and checked by the senior buyer before the first order.

observation.note: Quote the rule with its citation, e.g. (POL-PUR-001 §6.2). If a clause's status says it is replaced or not yet in force, follow the status. Stock, budgets and statuses come from Bahi.
